purpose: Stopped native DNS cleanup with immutable original receipts and authenticated A2 publication pins
changes: Add stopped-only round-dns-cleanup RPC; elapsed expiry permits recovery but never re-enables creation, DNS publication or rotation.
Use the existing setup journal and provider cleanup implementation without widening source-only setup mutation authority.

Retain initial DNS creation receipts. A2 alternatives require exact native execution/member/task lineage, authenticated publication binding, original record ID/marker, and the recorded provider wire request.
Prepared publication does not authorize the candidate address. Foreign values, altered markers, identity drift and uncertain ownership remain unresolved.
Persist an immutable selected cleanup pin and receipt digest before deletion. Repeat reads and resumed cleanup retain the same pin.
Reuse core publication authentication and action-journal validation without granting mutation or requiring fresh health after stop.
Extend protected runtime/application hashes and the unarmed bundle overlay for the cleanup dependencies.
limitations: The signed A2 cutover receipt is exercised through actual application services in SQLite unit tests with simulated provider responses. Linux full-application DNS teardown in this run only covers initial records, not an A2 cutover.
The Linux candidate reports and node bytes are synthetic; no actual node binary or cloud instance runs.
Private-material removal, controller-last teardown, complete host installation composition, native create-phase crash/elapsed expiry and assembled A1-to-A2 retry remain pending.
The recorded native_rpc_last_error is the intentionally injected source-delete reply loss, not an unhandled failure.
This component does not establish live readiness, complete the active goal or authorize a new real-machine run.
